review_type: Source-level category-99 actual-data check, not product regulatory approval

official_sources.name: 28 May 2020 FoSCoS order copied within 31 March 2022 SOP
Official source law, directions and amendments registry

seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.1 and FPSFA 3.1.1 + legally applicable additive permission/specification
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Exact chemical name, optical stereoisomer and CAS/INS identifiers as used
Grade, purity/impurity specification, supplier and batch documentation
Intended food use and dosage; correct Appendix A/other operative amendment by FPC
Applicable actual food additive permission, residual limits and accredited testing method
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: The 'L(+/-)' catalogue label does not prove which tartaric-acid stereoisomer or grade is used; never automatically assign a specific INS, purity/MRL or food-product category.

seven_records.product_name: Additives VA-VF of Nutraceutical Regulations excluding those already standardised
seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.1, original Nutraceutical Regulations and current legally effective directions/schedules
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Identify each additive's INS/CAS and technological function
Confirm which specific VA/VE/VF schedule entry and edition legally applies to the intended nutraceutical category
Reconcile 2016 schedules with later notified directions and amendments; do not transfer old numbering automatically
Purity, maximum levels and final product composition
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: The historic category title naming VA–VF does not itself prove the substance is permitted under all 2026 nutraceutical product routes or standard foods.

seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.1 category listing only until the exact legal chemical identity and source permission are established
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Supplier identity and complete chemical composition; any mixed alkali and salts
Exact INS/CAS where applicable, manufacturing process and food-grade purity
Explicit permission and intended technological function under legally effective standard
Laboratory COA, use level and applicable food-category limitations
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: Do not guess that 'Sajji Khar' always equals one salt (e.g., sodium carbonate) or inherit a single salt's additive limits by name.

seven_records.product_name: Permitted enzymes and their preparations excluding those already listed under Processing Aids and Nutraceutical Regulations
seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.2 distinct from 99.4 processing aids; FPSFA relevant enzyme/processing-aid permission
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Exact enzyme and EC number, production species and source (including GMM status if relevant)
Fermentation/manufacture, carrier and total organic solids; food-grade specification
Is it a direct enzyme preparation or processing aid under 99.4? Resolve actual use category and residues
Permitted application, intended target food and method to demonstrate applicable purity/safety
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: 99.2 listing excludes enzymes already covered under processing aids/nutraceutical routes. Do not treat 99.2 and 99.4 as interchangeable or infer use approval.

seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.3; FPSFA 3.3.1 flavouring agents and prohibited flavours
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Full component and carrier/solvent disclosure, natural/nature-identical/artificial route and identity
Screen every component against current 3.3.1 prohibited flavour substances and solvent restrictions
Food category, max levels/GMP conditions, powder anti-caking use, allergen/label requirements
Actual blend specification, batch COA and substance-specific traceability
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: A FoSCoS 99.3 premix cannot be treated as automatically permissible; Chapter 3.3.1 excludes explicitly prohibited flavour substances, and additive/solvent conditions apply.

seven_records.product_name: Ingredients listed under Schedule IV, Schedule VI and Schedule VIII of Nutraceutical Regulations
seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.7 functional ingredients; current Nutraceuticals Regulation/directions with schedule identity reconciliation
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Actual ingredient name, botanical species or chemical identity, extract/plant part and active marker
Which applicable schedule, issue date, any amended/new numbered schedule and conditions
Permitted product category, usage limits, botanical processing/standardization and restrictions
Supplier purity and safety evidence, correct Food Product Category and license route
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: The legacy category name lists Schedules IV, VI and VIII; never assume those schedule numbers or permissions are unmodified in newer nutraceutical directions.

seven_records.candidate_legislative_area: FoSCoS 99.7; each component's operative functional-ingredient/nutraceutical regulation
required_identity_and_use_evidence: Full component list, potency and ratio, excipients, carriers, color/flavour additives
Each active's notified legal entry/edition and maximum use in intended finished food
Extract part/source, purity markers, microbial/contaminant sampling and applicable claims
Actual manufacturer registered product and whether mixture is an ingredient vs final consumer product
seven_records.hard_stop_during_matching: Premix or blending does not create blanket permission. Every active, carrier, use and final category must be independently permitted.

guards: Category 99 is a FoSCoS licensing umbrella, not a universal single FSSR purity and finished-food contaminant standard.
For every 99.1 additive, verify exact chemical/INS/grade and the right target food permission; do not infer a compound from product label.
For 99.2 enzymes distinguish true enzyme ingredients from 99.4 processing aids and verify EC/source/target food.
For 99.3 flavour mixtures the Chapter 3.3.1 prohibited flavours and solvent restrictions must be screened component by component.
For 99.7 functional ingredient mixtures check each active, its relevant effective nutraceutical/functional-ingredient schedule and grade.
Never map a blank FSSR field to 2.12 proprietary status or to a generic Chapter 3 number and call it legally confirmed.
None of these research findings changes the original R50 product CTR legal article hold, or supplies actual lab/spec/label evidence.
